rationale: The title and abstract describe a theoretical critique of approaches to studying state bureaucracy and administrative reform in Latin America. It contains no mention of water or sanitation services, household/community service access outcomes, or empirical water/sanitation evidence, failing Criterion 1 (E01) as well as Criteria 3 and 4.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both readings exclude the record (E01): although the paper addresses general administrative reform and state bureaucracy (fitting broad institutional/administrative concepts), it is a purely theoretical macro-political/administrative essay with no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: Critical Notes for a Theory of State Bureaucracy
A critical review of historical-structural, administrative, & contextual approaches to the study of the institutional state apparatus
An attempt is made to reconstruct the paradigm implicit in the practice of administrative reform
